To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the spectral gap of a random reversible Markov matrix can be controlled by a tunable parameter, and the stationary distribution of such a Markov matrix can also be controlled by the same tunable parameter.

we have developed a method to construct random Markov matrices with desired properties, and that the extremal eigenvalues of these matrices can be tuned by a parameter $c$ that controls the spectral gap.

a random reversible Markov matrix with tunable extremals is obtained by adding a fixed constant $c>0$, which is the spectral gap, to the adjacency matrix of an Erd\H{o}rs-R\'enyi random graph, and normalizing its rows.
In summary, our research is concerned with
random Markov matrices whose ESDs are symmetric nondegenerate and whose extremal eigenvalues are tunable in a certain range.
the following question: how to sample random matrices with a tunably large spectral gap and a nondegenerately nonuniform stationary distribution.
the construction of random reversible Markov matrices whose spectral properties are tunable.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, given any $c>0$, $p\in [0,1]$, and $b\in (0,\frac{1}{\sqrt{1+c}})$, there is a random Markov matrix with the following properties: its stationary distribution is nonuniform, its spectral gap is tunable, and the ESD weakly concentrates around a nondegenerate distribution.
for $p\approx c$, the Markov matrix is close to the random walk on the complete graph, whereas for $p\ll c$ it is close to the lazy random walk on the empty graph.

the ESD of the normalized Markov matrix is a symmetric, nondegenerate distribution whose extremal eigenvalues other than 1 fall in the interval $[-1/\alpha, -\beta]\cup [\beta,1/\alpha]$, where $\alpha=1/\sqrt{c+1}$, $\beta=1/\sqrt{\alpha}$, and $0<\beta<\alpha<1$.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spectral properties of a random reversible Markov matrix with a nondegenerate ESD are controllable by a tunable constant $c>0$.
, by a simple random sampling, one can construct a large reversible Markov chain whose ESD is nondegenerate and whose spectral gap can be tuned.

, for $n$ large enough, the ESD of a normalized random Markov matrix is close to a symmetric distribution with the largest and smallest eigenvalue being $1$ and $-1/\sqrt{n}+O(1)$ in probability, and the spectral gap can be made arbitrarily large by choosing a large enough $c$.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the spectral gap of $A_n/n$ can be tuned to any $[0,1)$ by adding $c/n$ and normalizing its rows.
a Markov chain with the desired properties can be constructed from a random graph.
the spectral gap can be tuned from $1-\epsilon$ to $1-\delta$, where $\epsilon$ is arbitrarily small, by adding a constant to the entries of a random matrix.
